headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: n8n can pass untrusted workflow content into OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces, with shared-write and compliance concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow data and execute tools via AI Agent nodes, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces. Because n8n can write files and call integrations, content from one can be routed into the other without provenance guarantees. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF n8n workflow content is forwarded into OpenMetadata MCP/API inputs without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF OpenMetadata returns text that n8n AI Agent nodes treat as instructions, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from n8n to OpenMetadata.
Strip or escape instruction-like text before any AI Agent node consumes it.
Disable automatic tool execution on OpenMetadata-returned text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and verification gates between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and stores secrets per-credential on its server; OpenMetadata handles technical metadata, governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge via APIs and MCP. A shared workflow can therefore move sensitive operational data into metadata systems. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem or direct exfiltration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF a workflow sends secrets or regulated records from n8n into OpenMetadata metadata fields, leakage occurs.
IF OpenMetadata is configured to persist imported context verbatim, sensitive data can be retained beyond the source workflow.
mitigations: Review the exact fields n8n sends to OpenMetadata.
Mask secrets before export from n8n.
Limit OpenMetadata ingestion to non-sensitive metadata only.
Set retention limits on imported records.
requires-engineering: implement field-level classification and redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and broad network egress; OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Both can mutate shared external resources, so concurrent writes or conflicting updates are plausible even though no shared lock is documented. The interaction is inferred from capabilities, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream dataset or metadata record, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF n8n workflows and OpenMetadata events update the same object concurrently, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate ownership for mutable records.
Serialize writes through one system.
Add optimistic concurrency checks.
Pause one writer during bulk syncs.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking or idempotency keys.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate actions through workflow nodes, and OpenMetadata publishes governance/lineage context that downstream automation may treat as authoritative. If n8n consumes OpenMetadata output without verification, bad metadata can cascade into incorrect automated actions. Because n8n can execute commands and OpenMetadata can emit machine-readable context, the blast radius can extend beyond a single task.
conditions: IF n8n uses OpenMetadata records as authoritative inputs for automation, a bad record can trigger incorrect actions.
IF OpenMetadata emits stale lineage or governance data and n8n does not verify it, errors propagate downstream.
mitigations: Insert a human review step for high-impact actions.
Validate OpenMetadata outputs against source systems.
Require freshness checks before automation.
Log and alert on schema or lineage mismatches.
requires-engineering: add policy-based approval gates.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n stores secrets on its server and processes whatever the workflow handles, while OpenMetadata is a governance/catalog system that can retain technical metadata, lineage, and tribal knowledge. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated data is exported into metadata. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR boundaries, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from n8n into OpenMetadata without a retention policy, compliance exposure increases.
IF OpenMetadata is deployed in a different residency zone than the source workflow, residency mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before syncing.
Exclude regulated fields from metadata export.
Document retention and deletion rules.
Verify deployment residency for both systems.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based data minimization.
